sources.title: New York State Next Generation English Language Arts Learning Standards
sources.notes: Adopted September 2017. Grade-specific PK through 8; high-school bands 9–10 and 11–12. Source scope reviewed, not a complete teaching-text ingestion.

sources.title: Introduction to the New York State Next Generation English Language Arts Learning Standards
sources.notes: Explains grade and grade-band organization, lifelong literacy practices and PK–5 foundational reading. Official page/index content reviewed; exact file bytes not retained.

sources.title: Next Generation ELA Instruction and Assessment Implementation Timeline
sources.notes: Separates instruction implementation from assessment cutover; first Next Generation ELA Regents June 2026. Official page/index content reviewed; exact file bytes not retained.

sources.title: New York State K–8 Social Studies Framework
sources.notes: Framework adopted in 2014; K–8 revision March 2016. Contains grade-specific content and practices. Embedded legacy literacy passages must be read alongside later Next Generation literacy standards.

sources.title: New York State Grades 9–12 Social Studies Framework
sources.notes: Provides Global History I/II, United States History and Government, Participation in Government and Civics, and Economics, the Enterprise System, and Finance. Local curriculum and materials remain school decisions.

sources.title: Social Studies FAQ
sources.notes: Confirms framework implementation, local curriculum/material selection, PK–12 instruction, and locally approved AP government/economics equivalency.

sources.title: Resource Guides for School Success: The Prekindergarten Early Learning Standards
sources.notes: Consolidated four-year-old expectations across developmental domains; not a curriculum or assessment. Official page/index content reviewed; exact file bytes not retained.

sources.title: New York State Learning Standards for World Languages
sources.notes: Adopted March 15, 2021; July 2021 terminology change from LOTE. Modern and classical tracks have different numbering for interpersonal/presentational communication.

sources.title: World Languages Implementation Timeline
sources.notes: Revised standards required by grade 10 September 1, 2026, grade 11 September 2027 and grade 12 September 2028; earlier school adoption permitted. Elementary progression begins with the first offered language year.

sources.title: New York State Themes and Topics for World Languages
sources.notes: Modern-language table has four themes and 17 topics, with checkpoint-specific applicability. Classical-language themes are separate. This source guides contexts, not a universal language or grade sequence.

sources.title: World Languages Themes and Topics
sources.notes: Page contains an inconsistent Checkpoint C topic count; use the actual PDF table and review notes rather than encoding that count.

sources.title: Checkpoint A Assessment Guidance
sources.notes: First assessments required to match revised world-language standards were June 2025; modern, classical and ASL guidance are distinct.

sources.title: Checkpoint B Assessment Guidance
sources.notes: First required revised-standard Checkpoint B assessments June 2027. Current page places ASL with category 3–4, unlike the older category 1–2 target PDF; specialist review needed before assigning ASL targets.

sources.title: Proficiency Ranges and Performance Indicators for Modern Languages, Category 1–2
sources.notes: Older document says ASL targets match category 1–2, conflicting with April 2026 Checkpoint B page. Do not apply its ASL category automatically. Official page/index content reviewed; exact file bytes not retained.

sources.title: Academic and Linguistic Demands: Creating Access to Next Generation ELA for Linguistically Diverse Learners
sources.notes: Current instructional access resource extends the older Bilingual Common Core Progressions and supports grade-level ELA, language development and locally designed ENL/Home Language Arts curricula.

sources.title: Units of Study Tables for English as a New Language and Bilingual Education Programs
sources.notes: Links K–8 and 9–12 service tables and identifies ALDs as an access framework. This catalog does not determine statutory service minutes, placement or eligibility.

sources.title: Classroom Practices for Multilingual Learners and English Language Learners and the Next Generation ELA Learning Standards
sources.notes: PK–12 instructional examples; multilingual learners work toward the same Next Generation standards with appropriate language support. Examples are not a mandated curriculum.

sources.title: Joining the WIDA Consortium and New English Language Proficiency Assessments
sources.notes: Final NYSESLAT spring 2026; first ACCESS and Alternate ACCESS spring 2027; screeners replace NYSITELL in fall 2027. Explicitly preserves ALDs and Next Generation ELA instruction.

sources.title: WIDA: New York State Assessment Information
sources.notes: Official hub links the transition memo, New York partner guidance, and 2026–27 ACCESS preparation materials. HTML is a retrieval snapshot, not a teaching corpus.

sources.title: 2026 NYSESLAT School Administrator’s Manual
sources.notes: Historical/placement context for 2026–27: describes final NYSESLAT and its five levels. It does not establish a score conversion to WIDA or the 2027 assessment framework. Official page/index content reviewed; exact file bytes not retained.

sources.title: Next Generation Grades 6–12 Literacy Standards in History/Social Studies, Science and Technical Subjects
sources.notes: Actual reading/writing tables use bands 6–8, 9–10 and 11–12, despite introductory prose summarizing high school as 9–12. Embedded content literacy does not replace subject knowledge or general ELA.

sources.title: School Library Services FAQ
sources.notes: Identifies library/information-skills instruction in grades 7 and 8 and integration with classroom objectives; not a standalone K–12 numbered content standard.

sources.title: Media Literacy: A Toolkit for Educators
sources.notes: State educator toolkit hosted by NYSED; guidance/resource collection, not a new independently numbered statewide subject standard. Official page/index content reviewed; exact file bytes not retained.

sources.title: Early Learning Curriculum Guidance
sources.notes: Explains the distinction between state learning expectations and locally developed or selected curriculum. This general principle does not establish a full syllabus for any high-school elective.

sources.title: NY Inspires Transformation Timeline
sources.notes: Distinguishes adopted instructional changes from proposed graduation changes; current diploma requirements remain until Board approval.

sources.title: New York State Alternate Assessment
sources.notes: Eligible students use DLM for ELA, mathematics and science at reduced depth, breadth and complexity; eligibility and individualized teaching remain school decisions.

transitions.title: Next Generation ELA Regents cutover
transitions.finding: June 2026 is the first Next Generation ELA Regents administration; January 2026 was the last legacy administration. This is an assessment transition, not publication of a new annual curriculum.

transitions.title: World Languages revised standards reach grade 10
transitions.finding: Revised 2021 standards are required for grade 10 instruction by September 1, 2026; the first required aligned Checkpoint B assessment is June 2027. Grade is not a universal proficiency level.

transitions.title: World Languages grade 11 phase
transitions.finding: Mandatory grade 11 revised-standard implementation begins after the 2026–27 year; schools may adopt earlier. Preserve the school’s actual version.

transitions.title: World Languages grade 12 phase
transitions.finding: Mandatory grade 12 revised-standard implementation begins September 2028, completing K–12 alignment; do not represent it as universally completed in 2026–27.

transitions.title: ACCESS replaces annual NYSESLAT assessment
transitions.finding: Final NYSESLAT administration was spring 2026. First WIDA ACCESS and Alternate ACCESS administration is spring 2027. Instruction remains aligned to NY ALDs and Next Generation ELA; assessment adoption is not adoption of a replacement instructional curriculum.

transitions.title: English-language screener transition follows ACCESS
transitions.finding: NYSITELL continues until WIDA screeners are implemented in fall 2027. Do not replace the 2026–27 intake assessment prematurely or invent a score conversion.

review_notes.finding: 2026–27 labels applicability of reviewed authorities. New York has no single annually issued complete statewide teaching curriculum for all subjects. Schools select curriculum, texts, pacing and electives within requirements.

Short topic phrases are original scope summaries for planning and discovery. They are not full standard statements, numbered standards, approved student-facing lessons or evidence of complete corpus coverage.

ELA uses PK–8 grades and 9–10/11–12 bands; actual disciplinary-literacy tables use 6–8, 9–10 and 11–12; languages use checkpoints and language-specific proficiency. Do not fabricate a fixed annual sequence where the authority is banded or proficiency-based.

The source introduction summarizes bands as 6–8 and 9–12, but actual reading/writing standard tables separately label 6–8, 9–10 and 11–12. This catalog follows the table labels and does not merge away the high-school progression.

Social-studies framework PDFs retain older embedded Common Core literacy passages. Pair their subject content with the later 2017 Next Generation disciplinary literacy authority rather than silently treating the embedded text as current literacy alignment.

The official themes page states four themes and 17 modern topics but separately claims 18 topics at Checkpoint C. The exact 2021 PDF table has 17 topics; retain the table as evidence and do not encode the inconsistent HTML count.
Modern standard 2 is interpersonal and 3 presentational; classical standard 2 is presentational and 3 interpersonal. Track-specific numbering must remain intact.

The August 2021 category 1–2 proficiency document assigns ASL matching targets, while the April 2026 Checkpoint B page groups ASL with category 3–4. Require ASL-specific specialist review before assigning checkpoint targets or claiming complete proficiency coverage.

NYSED’s October 8, 2025 memo expressly preserves ALD and Next Generation ELA instruction while changing English-proficiency assessment. Do not infer adoption of WIDA ELD Standards as the school curriculum, replace the NY ALDs, or map old NYSESLAT levels to WIDA scores automatically.

Library/media-literacy scope draws from existing literacy expectations plus guidance. Library/information-skills instruction is identified for grades 7 and 8, and the January 2025 toolkit is not an independently numbered new K–12 subject standard.

Humanities electives are optional school offerings. Transferable literacy skills do not establish a full statewide psychology, sociology, philosophy, writing, journalism or debate syllabus. Require a reviewed local syllabus and corpus; external AP/IB/college frameworks remain separate.

The September 2026 timeline describes proposed diploma-assessment changes for fall 2027 and competency-based implementation for the 2029 entering cohort. It explicitly says existing graduation requirements remain until Board approval. Do not remove 2026–2027 requirements or treat the Portrait of a Graduate as a replacement subject syllabus.

Include accessible tutoring across the academic catalog. NYSAA/DLM is an eligibility-based alternate assessment pathway, not an automatic lower-grade curriculum or a diagnosis inferred from chat. A separately reviewed Essential Elements mapping and school-authorized individualized plan are needed before claiming alternate-pathway alignment.
